main_text.p: mus est, cum verba Juramenti aut Pro-missionis ita sunt clara, sive primò ex propria sua & communi significatione; sive fecundò ex recepto loquendi more alicuius gentis vel civitatis; sive tertiò ex mutuo consensu partium: ut de eorum sensu inter partes omnino constet. Exemplum Primi: Caius Titio, spondeo me fundum meum Tusculanum tibi daturum, si mihi infra mensem centum aureos dependeris. Exempla Secundi: Si Johannes cum Petro linguâ nostrâ vernaculâ sic contraheret, pro centum mar-cis quas tibi debeo, dabo tibi cras de gre-ge meo centum oves masculas, Anglicè Foz[?] an hundred markes an hundred pethers: vel, Pro usu-fructu fundi tui solvam tibi quotannis tres modios frumenti, Anglicè Thre[?] bushels of wheat. Quorum in priori exemplo, etsi voca-bulum illud An hundred fit ita ambigu-um, ut nunc idem significet quod Latinis proprie est (Centum, hoc est quinquies viginti, nunc majorem summam, &c. vicies viginti; tamen ex passim recepto per universum regnum Angliæ illius voluntatis usu, mens ita contrahentium sic effet manifesta[?], ut de sensu verborum nulla offet[?] oriri lis: quandoquidem An hun-dred,

page.notes: Several words in black letter are hard to read: "Foz" (first word of the English phrase), "Thre" and "manifesta" (initial letter cut off at the left edge). "offet" is read as "posset" from the context, but the scan shows only "offet", so it is marked [?]. "effet" is kept as printed. The line "quandoquidem An hun-dred," ends on a printed hyphen. Left edge of the page is trimmed, so the first word "mus" is a fragment. The "(Centum" bracket is printed as shown. The small specks in the margins are not printed text.
